text:
morgan: Heads up — I ran a quick sim of the prefetch quiesce path during node drain and hit a weird race where prefixes got marked demoted but KV lease stayed true.
neil: ugh, can you paste the minimal trace? short is fine
morgan: yep
morgan: ```
# simplified trace
1) client read -> lease held by nodeA
2) prefetch triggered -> nodeB asks to quiesce prefix
3) nodeA demotes prefix locally but does not release lease immediately
4) nodeB prefill assumes demoted state, writes resident metadata
5) client follows up -> sees stale tombstone -> wrong readpath
``` 
anya: interesting. sounds like we have a window where demote visibility != lease visibility
kevin: is this happening on soft-demote only or hard-demote too?
morgan: reprobed in both, but hard-demote turns into faster tombstone which made it more obvious. soft-demote just prolonged the inconsistent view long enough to hit a client retry
neil: my gut: we need a quiesce handshake that obsfucates prefill until lease is fully transferred or a fence token is advanced.
anya: agreed. alternatives: (A) make demote atomic with lease release (big refactor to ownership flow) (B) add quiesce token + prefill barrier (smaller, can be composable) (C) change prefill to validate lease epoch before committing resident metadata
kevin: (C) seems minimal. on prefill commit do a `lease_epoch == observed_epoch` check; if mismatch abort and fallback to shadow read
morgan: that would avoid wrong residency writes but add a roundtrip. cost ok? we prefill asynchronously so some retries are acceptable
neil: plus we need to ensure abort path doesn't leave partial metadata. either use CAS or write a transient marker then finalize. we already have generation-tagged writes for slabs.
anya: sketch of (B): quiesce token flow
anya: ```
1) nodeB requests quiesce token for prefix P
2) nodeA replies with token T that includes epoch E and fence
3) nodeB starts prefill but includes T in writes
4) nodeA only demotes after it publishes release event with same T
5) reads require T match or fallback
``` 
kevin: nice. token approach gives explicit coupling without making lease release synchronous. but we need to plumb token through placement and metrics and avoid token blowup
morgan: operationally, we also need backpressure when nodeA is slow to release — otherwise prefill will busyloop and increase cache churn
neil: put a soft TTL on token and use exponential backoff. also surface a metric: prefill_quiesce_wait_seconds
anya: another corner — multi-prefill where multiple nodes race to fill same prefix after an eviction. tokens help linearize but we need deterministic winner selection
kevin: winner: first writer with highest epoch or matching token. losers fallback to read-through
morgan: can we prototype (C) first? smaller surface area. then tack on token for perf if we see too many aborts
neil: +1. prototype checklist:
- add epoch check on prefill commit (quick)
- add abort handler that cleans partial resident writes
- add unit tests for demote+lease mismatch
- synthetic chaos test: drain node during heavy prefill
anya: I'll own the tests. kevin, can you sketch commit-change? maybe a small patch that CASes on prefix.residency.{epoch}
kevin: yep, I'll draft. will push a branch and tag `prefetch/quiesce-epoch-check` by EOD
prefetch-bot: new branch created: prefetch/quiesce-epoch-check -> link: https://git.internal/r/redwood/prefetch/quiesce-epoch-check
morgan: thanks. once we have metrics we can decide if token flow is necessary. leaving thread open for follow-ups and perf numbers
neil: also ping infra to run a canary with node drain during load. we want real latencies.
kevin: noted, will add canary config in the PR
morgan: :thumbsup:
